name: Badge Moss
description: Plagiomnium insigne, commonly known as Badge Moss or Coastal Leafy Moss, is a terrestrial moss native to western North America from southeastern Alaska to central California and as far east as western Montana. It belongs to the Mniaceae family and is the largest species in the genus Plagiomnium. It features large, showy plants with dark green to yellow-green leaves 3–11 mm long, elliptic to narrowly elliptic, with toothed margins. Leaves spread widely when moist and become shriveled when dry. It grows on humus, soil, or rotten logs in shaded forests (including redwood forests), swampy areas, and sometimes lawns, from sea level to subalpine. In terrariums it provides lush ground cover and a natural forest-floor look. Non-flowering; reproduces by spores.
careTips: Large, showy moss – distinctive among temperate mosses
Prefers shaded conditions – avoid direct sun which can dry it out
Requires very high humidity (70–90%) – ideal for closed terrariums
Keep consistently moist but not waterlogged – mist regularly
Cool to moderate temperatures (10–24°C) – native to temperate coastal regions
Grows on humus, soil, or wood – use moist, slightly acidic substrate
Non-toxic and safe for terrarium inhabitants
Propagates via spores or division – separate portions to spread
If moss turns brown or shrivels, increase humidity and misting
